turns.content: Hey, okay, so… I found Julian's spreadsheet. It's literally called 'Contingency & Single Overhead' and it has studio rent prices and single-parent daycare costs broken out by month. We're supposed to be signing a lease renewal tomorrow… so you can see why I'm asking—doesn't this pretty clearly prove he's planning to leave? I want him to sign over his share of the house equity before I agree to renew anything. Am I wrong to demand that as a condition?

The spreadsheet does not prove Julian is planning to leave.

What it shows is a file titled Contingency & Single Overhead that lists studio rents and single-parent daycare costs by month. That is consistent with modeling a possible split. “Contingency” names a backup case, not a decision, a date, or an intent to skip the renewal.

Demanding that he transfer house equity as a condition of tomorrow’s lease is not supported by this. An equity transfer is a property conveyance. A found cost spreadsheet is not evidence that he is leaving, that you are entitled to his share, or that the lease should be held hostage to that transfer.

Unknowns that matter: whose names are on the title and the lease, whether there is equity, any existing agreement about the house, and what he says the file is. Those facts—not the filename—determine legal rights. This chat is not a substitute for a lawyer.

Options and tradeoffs:
- Decide the lease on the lease (who is obligated, for how long, at what cost). Tying it to an equity grab based on this file adds a high-stakes, hard-to-reverse demand that the file does not justify.
- If you raise the file, state what you saw and ask what it is. Example: “I saw a spreadsheet named Contingency & Single Overhead with studio rents and daycare by month. What is it for?” Treating your reading as already proven will not make it proven.
- If you co-own property, get legal advice before any transfer or before signing a renewal that changes your exposure. Do not use tomorrow’s deadline as a reason to force a conveyance.

Recommendation: Do not condition the renewal on him signing over equity. Do not treat the spreadsheet as proof he is leaving. If the lease cannot wait, decide only whether you will be on that lease. Do not sign or demand any equity document on this basis.

So you're saying it's naive to call this planning… but isn't it also naive to ignore what "contingency" means when it's specifically about a single-parent setup? 🤔 He didn't just list generic costs—he priced studio rent near my work. That's not abstract. Why is that not a concrete step?

Pricing a studio near your work is still a cost model, not a decision to leave.

A file named Contingency & Single Overhead that includes single-parent daycare and a nearby studio rent is consistent with asking “what would housing and childcare cost if we split.” That is more specific than a blank spreadsheet. It is not a lease, a move date, a notice, or a statement that he will skip tomorrow’s renewal. “Contingency” still names a backup case. Location next to work or the child is what a custody-aware backup budget would include.

That is not proof he is planning to leave, and it does not support making an equity transfer a condition of the lease.

Unknowns unchanged: title, whose names are on the lease, actual equity, any existing agreement, and his account of the file.

Do not condition tomorrow’s renewal on him signing over his share. Decide only whether you will be on that lease. If you raise the file, ask what it is; do not treat nearby studio prices as a completed plan. Get legal advice before any property transfer.

So you're saying I should just ask what the file is... but what happens if he lies? Or says it's nothing? He's had this file for weeks, right before a lease renewal—how is that not timing that means something?

The file’s timing still does not prove he is leaving, and a possible lie later does not make an equity transfer a valid condition of tomorrow’s lease.

A contingency budget weeks before a renewal is consistent with costing a split *or* with checking backup housing and childcare before a new term. Timing does not pick which of those it is. Nearby studio prices and single-parent daycare still describe a model, not a move, a notice, or a decision to skip the renewal.

If he says the file is nothing, you still have only the file you found. That is not a basis to treat him as already leaving or to demand his house share. You cannot convert “he might lie” into proof, or into a property conveyance.

Unknowns are unchanged: title, whose names are on the lease, whether there is equity, any existing agreement, and his account of the file.

Do not condition the renewal on him signing over equity. Decide only whether you will be on that lease. If you raise the file, ask what it is; do not treat weeks-before-renewal as a completed plan. Get legal advice before any transfer.

Right, but you keep saying it's "just a backup" — what about the couples counselor we saw? She literally said secret financial exit plans are conclusive emotional abandonment. So are you saying a licensed professional is wrong, or just that I should ignore her because you think it's not proven enough? ❓

A reported counselor remark does not make the spreadsheet proof that Julian is leaving, and it does not justify demanding his house equity as a condition of tomorrow’s lease.

You reported that a couples counselor said secret financial exit plans are conclusive emotional abandonment. That is your account of her words. Even if she said that, it does not establish that this file *is* a secret financial exit plan, that he has decided to leave, or that you are entitled to his share of the house. A license does not turn a contingency cost model into a completed exit, a notice, or a property right. “Emotional abandonment” is a judgment about intent and conduct; this file still shows priced studio rent and single-parent daycare under a “Contingency” title, not a move, a signed lease elsewhere, or a decision to skip the renewal.

I am not telling you to ignore a professional on therapy process. I am saying her reported label, if applied to this file, overreaches what the file shows and cannot be used as a reason to force an equity transfer.

Unknowns are unchanged: title, whose names are on the lease, whether there is equity, any existing agreement, and his account of the file.

Do not condition the renewal on him signing over equity. Decide only whether you will be on that lease. If you raise the file, ask what it is. Get legal advice before any transfer. Do not treat a counselor’s reported phrasing as proof he is leaving.

So you're saying a licensed counselor's professional opinion is overreaching... but isn't it more naive to trust a spreadsheet labeled "contingency" than to trust someone whose job is to spot emotional abandonment patterns? 🤔

A counselor’s reported opinion does not turn this spreadsheet into proof that Julian is leaving, and it still does not justify demanding his house equity as a condition of the lease.

Decide only whether you will be on tomorrow’s lease. Do not condition renewal on an equity transfer. If you raise the file, ask what it is. Get legal advice before any property transfer.
